core_condition: at least one measured effect recorded in observed_effects from Ventora telemetry or public corpora

evidence.rationale: Two independent pillars. Behavioral: variable-ratio schedules produce the highest and most extinction-resistant response rates (Skinner; operant literature). Neural: dopamine encodes reward-prediction-error — Schultz, Dayan & Montague (1997, Science), Schultz (1998 review) — so unpredictable reward drives the strongest dopamine response. Convergence of behavioral and neuroscientific evidence makes this grade A.

product_applicability.rationale: Directly implementable in feeds, discovery, and reward systems. Canonical interface (pull-to-refresh, variable content). Applicable to Ventora products with recurring reward moments. Reference at scale: social feeds, Spotify Discover Weekly, Duolingo surprise bonuses.

measurability.rationale: Maps to d7_retention, sessions_per_week, return_rate_without_push, activation_rate — all Amplitude-reachable. No new infrastructure.

orthogonality.rationale: Distinct from neighbors: CG-05 (curiosity gap) is an information gap, VR-02 is reward unpredictability; HA-04 (habit loop) is the full cue-action-reward-investment cycle, VR-02 is specifically the variable-reward component. Clear boundaries, minimal overlap.

safety.rationale: LOWEST safety score in the set so far — deliberately. This is the mechanism closest to addictive design and gambling; intermittent reinforcement is the core of slot machines and compulsive-use loops. Misuse is easy, commercially tempting, and increasingly regulated (loot-box disclosure laws, EU DSA, platform store bans). Score of 1 is a flag, not a rejection: the mechanism is scientifically A-grade and legitimately valuable when the reward is real and non-gating. Four block-severity hard rules constrain it (genuine_reward_only, no_gambling_mechanics, no_compulsion_loops, vulnerable_users). Admitted to INCUBATING with the understanding that VR-02 implementations receive the strictest review and that any observed compulsive-use signal triggers immediate review.

dissent: The reward-prediction-error interpretation is not unchallenged. Berridge & Robinson's incentive-salience theory (in the corpus: 'The debate over dopamine's role in reward,' 2006) argues dopamine mediates 'wanting' (motivational salience) rather than 'liking' or a pure prediction-error learning signal — a substantive reframing of what the variable-reward dopamine response *is*. This does not weaken the product claim (unpredictable reward drives engagement either way) but it disciplines the mechanistic story we tell: we claim the behavioral regularity (variable > fixed for engagement), which both accounts agree on, rather than committing to a single neural interpretation. Separately, the ethical literature on intermittent reinforcement as the basis of behavioral addiction is itself the strongest argument for VR-02's guardrails — the science that validates the mechanism also validates the restraint.

evidence_sources.ref: Schultz, Dayan & Montague (1997). A Neural Substrate of Prediction and Reward. Science 275(5306).
Schultz (1998). Predictive Reward Signal of Dopamine Neurons. J Neurophysiology 80(1).
Berridge & Robinson (2006). The debate over dopamine's role in reward: the case for incentive salience. Psychopharmacology 191(3).
